notes: Read SKILL.md (578 lines) in full; it is the only file. Operational security guidance for a Next.js/Clerk/Convex app: a decision guide for when to apply rate limiting and CSRF, environment-variable and secret-generation practices, startup config validation, a pre-deployment checklist, post-deployment monitoring signals and alert thresholds, and a daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly maintenance schedule.

Risk is medium because the checklists and quick-reference commands have the agent run `npm audit`, `npm outdated`, `npm update` (changes dependencies), `npm run build` / `NODE_ENV=production npm start`, `curl -I` against the user's deployed site, and generate local secrets with node's crypto (SKILL.md:127-133, 257-273, 503-553). Each acts on the user's own project and deployment, and nothing reads, prints, or transmits existing secrets (the grep checks only look for hardcoded key prefixes), so this is acceptable.

Template dependence: the middleware decision guide refers to withRateLimit()/withCsrf() from the Secure Vibe Coding OS starter, and the checklist calls starter files `scripts/test-rate-limit.js`, `scripts/security-check.sh`, `app/api/csrf/route.ts`, `docs/security/SECURITY_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (SKILL.md:214, 248, 268, 456, 463-473, 509, 537-538) that are not included. The decisions (which routes need rate limiting/CSRF/auth), env-var practices, monitoring and maintenance guidance still apply in any project; those script steps will simply be unavailable outside the starter.

Minor caveats: the decision matrix marks public read-only APIs as needing no rate limit (SKILL.md:65), unlike other skills in the collection; `clientIp` in the logging example has no guidance on trusted-proxy IP derivation; `git status | grep .env.local` will not show an ignored file. Reference links to OWASP, Next.js, Clerk, Convex, Stripe and header scanners are documentation only.
